note: What the title screen's destination cards say, in a travel guide's voice: one line that sells the place, three sights to see, one local custom and the best time to come. pipeline/build_scene.py write_index merges it into web/data/cities.json. Keep it about the place, not the data behind the model.

queenstown.line: The adventure capital of the south, folded between Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables. Ride the gondola up at dusk, watch the lake turn to gold, and be on the wharf when the old steamer whistles.
spots: Up to Bob's Peak, the whole lake beneath you
A 1912 coal-fired steamer, still sailing every day
A jagged wall of rock across the water, snow-capped till spring
local: Kāi Tahu named the bay Tāhuna. Today it's a burger after midnight and a Central Otago pinot on the waterfront.

sydney.line: A harbour city of sails and sandstone. Take the ferry past the Opera House, wander The Rocks where the colony began, and watch the bridge light up as the sun goes down behind Balmain.
spots: Utzon's white sails on Bennelong Point
The Coathanger: fly beneath its steel arch
Green-and-gold ferries out to Manly and Taronga
local: Gadigal Country for tens of thousands of years. Today: a flat white at dawn, a ferry to work, fish and chips on the quay.

kyoto.hook: Kyoto Tower's beacon, Nishiki Market and the Imperial Palace gardens

higashiyama.hook: Kiyomizu's wooden stage and lantern-lit stone lanes to the Yasaka Pagoda

fushimi-inari.hook: Ten thousand vermilion torii climbing the rice god's sacred mountain

tetsugaku.hook: A canal walk under the cherry trees, Ginkaku-ji to Nanzen-ji

whitsundays.hook: Whitehaven's pure silica sand swirling into the turquoise of Hill Inlet

hardy-reef.hook: Heart Reef from the air, the outer reef from the pontoon

green-island.hook: A rainforest cay off Cairns: snorkel straight off the beach

heron-island.hook: Green turtles nesting on a cay on the Tropic of Capricorn

lady-elliot-island.hook: Manta rays gliding at the reef's southern tip

lake-pukaki.hook: Aoraki / Mount Cook over a lake of glacial milk-blue

lake-tekapo.hook: A little stone church on the turquoise shore, under the stars

milford-sound.hook: A ship under mile-high walls, a waterfall straight into the sea
milford-sound.line: The fiord Kipling called the eighth wonder: Mitre Peak rising 1,690 m straight from the water, rainforest clinging to the rock, and falls that never stop.
spots: 1,690 m straight out of the fiord
151 m into the sea, a rainbow in its spray
Ride the ship out to the Tasman Sea
local: Rata in flower at Christmas, a rainbow in the spray of Stirling Falls, and gulls behind the boat.

new-york.line: The city that never sleeps: Lower Manhattan's canyons, the Statue of Liberty across the harbour, and a slice at midnight.

london.line: Two thousand years on the Thames: St Paul's dome, the Tower's ravens, and a pint in the City when the bells ring out.

singapore.line: The garden city on the equator: Marina Bay's skyline, the Supertrees at night, and chilli crab at a hawker centre.

Kyoto.line: Japan's capital for a thousand years, and it still keeps the old hours: temple bells at dawn, lanterns in the lanes at dusk, and some 1,600 temples tucked between the hills.
local: Matcha and wagashi in a wooden machiya teahouse, and a maiko's footsteps on Gion's stones at dusk.

Kyoto Station.line: The glass valley of Kyoto Station, its 171 steps to the sky garden, and Kyoto Tower's candle across the road.

Higashi Honganji.line: One of the largest wooden halls in the world, a short walk from the station, and its hair rope still on show.

Shijo · Nishiki Market.line: Kyoto's kitchen: pickles, tofu and grilled skewers down a narrow covered market, a few streets from the Kamo River.

Nijo Castle.line: The shoguns' castle in the emperor's city: painted gold rooms and floors that sing like nightingales.

Imperial Palace.line: A thousand years of emperors behind long earthen walls, and Gyoen's gravel avenues under plum and cherry.

Gion · Yasaka Shrine.line: The vermilion Romon at the end of Shijo-dori, the lanterns of the dance hall, and Gion's lanes beyond.

Yasaka Pagoda.line: Five storeys over the tiled roofs: the pagoda every photograph of old Kyoto is framed around.

Ninenzaka · Sannenzaka.line: Stone steps between wooden teahouses and pottery shops, lantern-lit at dusk, all the way up to Kiyomizu.

Kiyomizu-dera.line: The wooden stage on its lattice of keyaki pillars, thirteen metres over the trees, and the Otowa spring below.

Fushimi Inari Taisha.line: The Romon guarded by stone foxes, and the two tunnels of the Senbon Torii climbing into the woods.

Yotsutsuji · Mount Inari.line: Halfway up Mount Inari through thousands of torii, the whole city spread out below at the crossroads.

Ginkaku-ji.line: The Silver Pavilion that was never silvered, its sand cone and its moss garden under the eastern hills.

Philosopher's Path.line: Two kilometres of stone path along a canal under cherry trees, the walk a philosopher took every morning.

Nanzen-ji.line: The great Sanmon gate, a red-brick aqueduct running through a Zen temple, and the old Keage Incline.

Tokyo.line: Thirty-seven million people, and every station opens onto a different world. Pick a stop on the line and step out into it.
local: The last train at midnight, an onigiri from the konbini, and a city that is still wide awake.

Marunouchi.line: Red-brick Tokyo Station, glass towers and the moats and stone walls of the Imperial Palace.

Ginza.line: Tokyo's grand boulevard: flagship stores, Wako's clock tower and the water bus down to Tokyo Tower.

Shibuya.line: The world's busiest crossing, the faithful dog Hachiko, and the whole city at your feet from SHIBUYA SKY.

Harajuku.line: Crepes and street fashion on Takeshita Street, and the hush of Meiji Jingu's forest next door.

Shinjuku.line: Neon Kabukicho, Golden Gai's six-seat bars, and the towers of Nishi-Shinjuku lit up at night.

Yotsuya.line: Quiet backstreets, a ginkgo avenue turning gold, and the Suga Shrine stairs from Your Name.

Sangen-jaya.line: Old izakaya alleys in the Sankaku Chitai, a corner bathhouse, and the Tokyo the tour buses miss.

Akihabara.line: Electric Town: arcades stacked six floors high, anime shops and maid cafés under the neon.

Asakusa.line: Old Edo: the Thunder Gate's great red lantern, incense smoke at Senso-ji, and rice crackers fresh off the grill.

Oshiage · Skytree.line: Tokyo Skytree, 634 m, the tallest tower in the world, rising over the Sumida River.

Ueno.line: Museums under the cherry trees, the lotus pond, and Ameyoko's market stalls beneath the tracks.

Ikebukuro.line: Sunshine City, Otome Road's anime shops and a bowl of ramen long after the last train.

Jinbocho.line: Book town: a hundred and more second-hand bookshops, and curry houses for when the browsing is done.

Roppongi.line: Art by day and clubs till dawn: the view from Mori Tower and the giant spider Maman.

Tsukishima.line: Monja Street: griddles sizzling in a riverside island town of old wooden houses.

Odaiba.line: Rainbow Bridge across the bay, a life-size Gundam, and a beach with the skyline beyond.

Shinagawa.line: The Tokaido's first stop: bullet trains, and Sengaku-ji where the forty-seven ronin rest.

Great Barrier Reef.line: The largest living thing on Earth: 2,300 km of coral off Queensland. Swim with turtles, walk silica sand as white as snow, and fly over Heart Reef.
local: Reef-safe sunscreen, fins kept off the coral, and a turtle always has right of way.

Mackenzie.line: Glacier-blue lakes under New Zealand's highest peak, and a night sky so dark it's protected as a reserve for the stars.
local: Lupins in early summer, the Milky Way overhead, and silence at the Church of the Good Shepherd.
